fixSteps.title: Clean Fuser Roller Path
fixSteps.instruction: Remove any debris or wrapped paper from around the fuser rollers. Ensure both rollers spin smoothly.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fuser or Motor
fixSteps.instruction: If rollers spin freely but the error persists, the motor or motor driver has failed and needs professional replacement.

whenToCallPro: If the fuser motor or DC controller board needs replacement, professional service is recommended.

faq.q: Is 59.05 related to the main motor errors?
faq.a: No, 59.05 is specifically the fuser motor, while 59.00-59.04 relate to the main drum motor. They are separate motor systems.

faq.q: Can a paper wrap cause this error?
faq.a: Yes, paper wrapped around a fuser roller creates a mechanical load that can prevent the motor from reaching speed.

title: Main Cooling Fan Error
shortDescription: The main cooling fan has failed or is not spinning at the correct speed.
fullDescription:
Error 57.05 indicates the main cooling fan in the printer is not operating correctly. The cooling fan is essential for maintaining safe operating temperatures inside the printer, particularly around the fuser and electronic components.

When the fan fails, the printer shuts down to prevent overheating damage. Common causes include dust buildup blocking the fan, a failed fan motor, or a disconnected fan cable.

The 57.XX family of errors covers various fans in the printer. The specific sub-code identifies which fan is affected: 57.01 is typically the main fan, 57.02 is the sub-fan, and 57.03-57.05 vary by model.

causes.cause: DC controller board fan circuit failure

fixSteps.title: Power Off and Inspect Vents
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off and unplug the printer. Check all ventilation openings for dust buildup or blockages.

fixSteps.title: Clean Fan and Vents
fixSteps.instruction: Use compressed air to blow dust out of the ventilation openings and fan area. If accessible, gently clean fan blades with a soft brush.

fixSteps.title: Check Fan Cable
fixSteps.instruction: If you can access the internal fan, verify the cable connection to the DC controller board is secure.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fan
fixSteps.instruction: If the fan does not spin after cleaning and cable check, replace the fan assembly. Order the specific fan part for your printer model.

whenToCallPro: If the fan motor is failed and internal disassembly is beyond your comfort level.

faq.q: Can dust really cause this error?
faq.a: Yes, heavy dust accumulation can physically prevent the fan from spinning, which the printer detects as a fan failure.

faq.q: Is it safe to use the printer with a failed fan?
faq.a: No. The printer disables itself for good reason. Operating without cooling can damage the fuser, electronics, and other internal components.

title: Environmental Sensor Error
shortDescription: The printer's environmental temperature or humidity sensor is reporting abnormal readings.
fullDescription:
Error 54.02 indicates the printer's environmental sensor is reporting values outside the expected range. This sensor measures ambient temperature and humidity to help the printer adjust fuser temperature and toner application settings.

Abnormal readings can be caused by a failed sensor, extreme environmental conditions (very hot, cold, or humid locations), or electrical interference. The printer uses this data to optimize print quality for the current environment.

If the printer is in an extreme environment, moving it to a climate-controlled room may resolve the error without any repair.

causes.cause: Printer located in extreme temperature environment
DC controller board sensor circuit fault

symptoms: Printer refuses to start in extreme conditions

fixSteps.title: Check Environment
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the printer is in a room with temperature between 15-30°C (59-86°F) and humidity between 20-80%. Move the printer if outside these ranges.

fixSteps.title: Allow Acclimatization
fixSteps.instruction: If the printer was recently moved from a very different environment, let it sit powered off for 2-4 hours to reach room temperature.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the printer, unplug for 5 minutes, then restart. The sensor may have given a transient false reading.

fixSteps.title: Sensor Replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If the error persists in a normal environment, the sensor requires professional replacement on the DC controller board.

whenToCallPro: If the error persists after ensuring proper environmental conditions and power cycling.

faq.q: What is the ideal environment for a laser printer?
faq.a: Most HP LaserJets operate best at 17-25°C (63-77°F) with 30-70% relative humidity.

faq.q: Can condensation cause this error?
faq.a: Yes, if a printer is moved from a cold to warm environment, condensation can form on the sensor and trigger false readings. Let it acclimatize.

title: DC Controller Communication Error
shortDescription: The DC controller board has lost communication with the formatter board.
fullDescription:
Error 55.02 indicates a communication failure between the printer's DC controller board and the formatter board. The DC controller manages all physical operations (motors, fuser, sensors) while the formatter handles data processing and network communication.

When these two boards cannot communicate, the printer cannot function. This error can be caused by a loose cable between the boards, a failed DC controller, a failed formatter, or electrical damage from a power surge.

The 55.XX error family covers various DC controller issues. 55.01 is typically a DC controller memory error, while 55.02 indicates an inter-board communication failure.

causes.cause: Loose cable between formatter and DC controller

symptoms: 55.02 error on display or blinking LEDs

fixSteps.title: Full Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the printer from the wall outlet for 5 minutes, then plug directly into a wall outlet (not a power strip) and power on.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Formatter Board
fixSteps.instruction: With the printer unplugged, locate the formatter board (usually accessible from the rear with a metal cover). Remove the screws, pull out the formatter, and firmly reseat it.

fixSteps.title: Check Internal Cables
fixSteps.instruction: With covers removed, inspect the ribbon cable connecting the formatter to the DC controller. Reseat both ends firmly.

fixSteps.title: Board Replacement
fixSteps.instruction: If reseating does not help, either the DC controller or formatter board needs replacement. Professional diagnosis is recommended.

whenToCallPro: If reseating cables and boards does not resolve the error, professional board-level diagnosis is needed.

faq.q: Is this error repairable?
faq.a: Often yes. Loose cables are the most common cause. If a board is truly failed, replacement boards are available from HP and third-party suppliers.

faq.q: Can a power surge cause this?
faq.a: Yes, power surges can damage the formatter or DC controller. Use a surge protector to prevent future occurrences.

title: Laser Scanner Beam Detect Error
shortDescription: The laser scanner cannot detect the beam, preventing image formation.
fullDescription:
Error 51.20 indicates the laser/scanner assembly's beam detect sensor cannot detect the laser beam. The laser scanner is responsible for writing the toner image onto the photoconductor drum using a precisely controlled laser beam.

When the beam detect sensor fails to see the laser, it can mean the laser diode has failed, the rotating mirror (polygon mirror) is not spinning, or the beam path is obstructed by dirt or debris.

This error prevents all printing as no image can be formed on the drum without the laser. The 51.XX errors all relate to the laser/scanner assembly, with different sub-codes indicating specific failure modes.

causes.cause: Dirty laser scanner mirror or lens

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the printer, unplug for 5 minutes, then restart. Transient errors may clear.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Toner Cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reseat the toner cartridge. On some models, the cartridge shutter interacts with the laser path and a misaligned cartridge can block the beam.

fixSteps.title: Check Laser Scanner
fixSteps.instruction: If accessible, carefully clean the laser scanner glass/mirror with a lint-free cloth. This component is inside the printer and may require panel removal.

fixSteps.title: Replace Laser Scanner
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning does not resolve the error, the laser/scanner assembly needs professional replacement.

whenToCallPro: If the laser scanner assembly or laser diode has failed, professional replacement is required.

faq.q: Is a laser scanner expensive to replace?
faq.a: Laser scanner assemblies range from $80-200 depending on the model. Labor adds $100-200 for professional installation.

faq.q: Can I keep using the printer?
faq.a: No, a 51.20 error completely prevents printing. The laser is essential for forming images on the drum.

title: Printhead Problem Detected
shortDescription: The printer has detected a problem with the installed printhead.
fullDescription:
Error 0xc4eb827a indicates the printer has detected an issue with the printhead assembly. This can range from a simple contact issue to a complete printhead failure requiring replacement.

The printhead is the component that physically deposits ink onto paper through microscopic nozzles. When the printer detects abnormal readings from the printhead's electrical contacts or nozzle health sensors, it triggers this error.

This error commonly appears after installing a new printhead, after a long period of non-use (dried ink in nozzles), or when the printhead has reached end of life.
symptoms: Printhead error message in HP Smart app
Horizontal lines or banding in prints

fixSteps.title: Clean Printhead Contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the printhead and gently clean the copper electrical contacts with a lint-free cloth dampened with distilled water. Also clean the matching contacts inside the printer.

fixSteps.title: Run Printhead Cleaning
fixSteps.instruction: Reinstall the printhead and run the deep cleaning function from the printer menu or HP Smart app. Run up to 3 cycles.

fixSteps.title: Soak Printhead Nozzles
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the printhead and place the nozzle plate face-down in a shallow dish of warm distilled water for 15 minutes to dissolve dried ink.

fixSteps.title: Replace Printhead
fixSteps.instruction: If cleaning does not resolve the error, purchase a replacement printhead for your specific printer model.

whenToCallPro: If the printhead and contacts are clean but the error persists, the printer's printhead carriage electronics may be faulty.

faq.q: How long does a printhead last?
faq.a: HP printheads typically last 2-5 years depending on usage. Regular printing keeps nozzles clear and extends printhead life.

faq.q: Does not using the printer damage the printhead?
faq.a: Yes, extended periods of non-use allow ink to dry in the nozzles, which can permanently clog them. Print at least once a week to maintain nozzle health.

title: Supply Problem - Cartridge Not Recognized
shortDescription: One or more ink or toner cartridges are not being recognized by the printer.
fullDescription:
The Supply Problem error indicates the printer cannot recognize or communicate with one or more installed ink or toner cartridges. This is a generic error that can appear on both inkjet and laser HP printers.

Common causes include non-genuine cartridges being blocked by HP's cartridge authentication system, dirty cartridge contacts, a cartridge installed in the wrong slot, or a defective cartridge. HP firmware updates sometimes change cartridge compatibility requirements.

This error can also appear when using refilled cartridges, as the memory chip may not have been properly reset after refilling.
symptoms: Orange or amber light on cartridge indicator

fixSteps.title: Verify Cartridge Placement
fixSteps.instruction: Remove all cartridges and verify each is installed in the correct color-coded slot. Reinstall firmly until each clicks.

fixSteps.title: Clean Contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Remove each cartridge and gently clean the copper or gold contacts with a dry lint-free cloth. Clean the matching printer contacts as well.

fixSteps.title: Try Genuine HP Cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: If using third-party cartridges, test with genuine HP cartridges. HP firmware may block non-genuine supplies.

fixSteps.title: Disable Cartridge Protection
fixSteps.instruction: On some models, go to Settings > Supply Settings > Cartridge Protection and disable it. Also check if HP Cartridge Policy is set to HP only and change if needed.

whenToCallPro: If genuine HP cartridges still show supply problems after cleaning, the cartridge contact assembly inside the printer may need replacement.

faq.q: Can HP block third-party cartridges?
faq.a: Yes, HP uses dynamic security to verify cartridge authenticity. Firmware updates may change which cartridges are accepted.

faq.q: How do I disable cartridge protection?
faq.a: Navigate to the printer's Settings > Supply Settings menu. Look for Cartridge Protection and Cartridge Policy options and set them to allow all cartridges.

title: Low Fuser Temperature Error
shortDescription: The fuser failed to reach operating temperature within the expected time.
fullDescription:
Error 50.10 indicates the fuser did not reach its target warm-up temperature within the allotted period during initialization. The DC controller monitors the fuser thermistor and flags this error when temperature rise is too slow.

Common causes include a damaged fuser heating element, a failed thermistor, loose fuser connectors, or a low AC line voltage supplying the printer. This error often appears after a printer has been stored in a cold location and may require multiple power cycles to clear.

On LaserJet Enterprise models, 50.10 is typically the precursor to replacing the fuser maintenance kit.

causes.cause: Failed fuser heating element or lamp

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the printer and unplug it for 10 minutes. Plug into a different outlet and power on.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Open the rear cover, release the green fuser handles, remove and reinstall the fuser ensuring it clicks fully into place.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fuser
fixSteps.instruction: If the error persists, replace the fuser assembly using the correct maintenance kit for your model.

whenToCallPro: If a replacement fuser also shows 50.10, the DC controller or low-voltage power supply may be at fault.

faq.q: Is the fuser safe to touch?
faq.a: Wait 30 minutes after printing before handling. The fuser operates above 180C and can cause severe burns.

faq.q: Can I reset 50.10 without replacing parts?
faq.a: Sometimes a long power-off period clears a transient error, but a persistent 50.10 usually means the fuser has failed.

title: Laser Beam Detect Error
shortDescription: The laser scanner did not generate a beam detect signal.
fullDescription:
Error 51.1 indicates the laser/scanner assembly failed to produce a beam detect (BD) signal within the required timing window. The BD signal is used by the DC controller to synchronize each laser scan line with the rotating polygon mirror.

Causes include a failed laser diode, dirty or damaged BD mirror, a scanner motor that is spinning but out of spec, or a broken flat cable connecting the laser unit to the DC controller. The error stops all printing immediately and requires scanner service.

On color LaserJets, 51.1 can specify which color laser unit (K, Y, M, C) has failed.

causes.cause: Damaged flat cable to DC controller

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the printer off for 2 minutes then power on.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Cables
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and reseat the flat cables between the laser/scanner and the DC controller board.

fixSteps.title: Replace Laser Scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the laser/scanner assembly with an OEM unit matching your model.

whenToCallPro: Laser alignment is critical. Professional service is recommended on color LaserJets.

faq.q: Can the laser harm my eyes?
faq.a: Never power the printer with the laser assembly removed. The invisible infrared beam can cause permanent eye damage.

title: Scanner Motor Startup Failure
shortDescription: The laser scanner motor failed to reach its operating speed.
fullDescription:
Error 52.0 is reported when the laser scanner motor does not reach its target rotational speed within the allotted startup period. The polygon mirror needs to spin at several thousand RPM to deflect the laser across the drum.

Causes include a seized bearing in the scanner motor, a failed motor driver on the DC controller, loose connectors, or a debris-blocked polygon mirror. The error can be intermittent if bearings are marginal.

The scanner motor is part of the laser/scanner assembly and is not typically serviced separately on newer HP LaserJets.

causes.cause: Failed motor driver on DC controller

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Power off for 5 minutes and then restart.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Scanner Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Access the top cover and reseat the scanner motor connector on the DC controller.

fixSteps.title: Replace Scanner Assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new OEM laser scanner assembly.

whenToCallPro: If the replacement scanner also fails to spin, the DC controller must be replaced.

faq.q: Can I lubricate the scanner motor?
faq.a: No. The bearings are sealed and any attempt to lubricate will likely make things worse.

title: DIMM Memory Error
shortDescription: A memory DIMM failed a startup self-test or is incompatible.
fullDescription:
Error 53.10 indicates a failure of the printer's memory DIMM during initialization. The formatter tests memory on every boot; when a bank fails the read/write test or the ID EEPROM cannot be read, a 53.xx error is issued.

Common causes include a loose DIMM, an incompatible third-party module, corrosion on the contacts, or a genuine memory failure. The printer may still start with a subset of memory but cannot process complex jobs.

53.10 corresponds to the first slot; 53.20 and higher indicate other slots.

fixSteps.title: Reseat DIMM
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, open the formatter cover, remove the DIMM and reseat it firmly.

fixSteps.title: Clean Contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Gently erase the gold contacts with a clean pencil eraser and reinsert.

fixSteps.title: Replace DIMM
fixSteps.instruction: Install a compatible HP-approved DIMM matching your model specs.

whenToCallPro: If reseating and replacement both fail the formatter board is likely at fault.

faq.q: Are third-party DIMMs safe?
faq.a: HP printers tolerate many generic DIMMs, but strict ECC and PC133 specs are required. Check your service manual.

title: DC Controller Communication Error
shortDescription: The formatter lost communication with the DC controller.
fullDescription:
Error 55.0 means the formatter cannot establish or maintain communication with the DC controller board. The DC controller manages all low-level engine functions, so the printer cannot operate without it.

Typical causes are a failed DC controller, a damaged flat cable between the formatter and DC controller, a failed formatter, or a firmware corruption. The error is persistent and typically displays immediately after the self-test passes.

A cold boot sometimes clears a transient 55.0, but recurring errors require hardware replacement.

fixSteps.title: Cold Boot
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 15 minutes then power on.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Cables
fixSteps.instruction: Open covers and reseat all cables between the formatter and DC controller.

fixSteps.title: Update Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: If the printer boots, apply the latest firmware from HP's support site.

fixSteps.title: Replace DC Controller
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new DC controller with matching part number.

whenToCallPro: DC controller swaps require firmware matching and mechanical alignment. Recommend professional service.

faq.q: Can firmware be the cause?
faq.a: Yes. A failed firmware update can leave the formatter unable to talk to the engine, producing 55.0.

title: Incorrect Paper Size Input Device
shortDescription: The printer detected an unsupported paper source or envelope feeder.
fullDescription:
Error 56.0 occurs when the printer detects a request to print from a paper input device that is missing, unsupported, or reporting a wrong paper size. It can also appear when the output delivery path is misconfigured.

Common scenarios include selecting a tray that is not installed, using an envelope feeder accessory that has been removed, or attempting to print to a stacker/stapler that is offline. The error is usually cleared by selecting a valid tray and resending the job.

fixSteps.title: Select Valid Tray
fixSteps.instruction: In the print driver pick a tray that is physically installed and loaded with paper.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Accessory
fixSteps.instruction: Reseat any envelope feeder, duplexer or output stacker attached to the printer.

whenToCallPro: Rarely required. Only if a tray sensor is physically damaged.

faq.q: Can I ignore this error?
faq.a: No, the job will not print until a valid input source is selected.

title: Main Cooling Fan Failure
shortDescription: The main cooling fan is not running or is rotating below its target speed.
fullDescription:
Error 57.1 indicates the main cooling fan failed to reach target RPM reported by its tachometer. The main fan cools the fuser area and internal electronics.

Causes include a seized fan bearing, dust buildup, a disconnected fan cable, or a failed fan driver on the DC controller. Ignoring the error can lead to thermal shutdown or fuser damage.

The fan is inexpensive and typically user-replaceable in 20-30 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clean Fan Grille
fixSteps.instruction: Use compressed air to blow out the intake and exhaust vents.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Open the side cover and verify the fan spins freely. Reseat its connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Fit an OEM replacement fan with matching part number.

whenToCallPro: If the fan driver circuit is blown, replace the DC controller via professional service.

faq.q: Can I keep using the printer?
faq.a: No. Running without cooling will shorten the life of the fuser and can cause thermal shutdowns.

title: Cartridge Area Fan Failure
shortDescription: The fan cooling the toner cartridge area failed.
fullDescription:
Error 57.6 indicates the cartridge cooling fan or the cartridge duct fan is not reporting correct speed. Without this fan, toner can melt inside the cartridge and blur prints.

Causes mirror other fan errors: seized bearings, disconnected cables, or driver failure. The fix is typically a fan swap.

fixSteps.title: Verify Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and remove the cartridge cover to access the fan. Spin it by hand to check for resistance.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fan
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new cartridge fan.

whenToCallPro: If the DC controller driver is blown.

faq.q: Does this damage the cartridge?
faq.a: Prolonged operation can cause toner to clump inside the cartridge, shortening its life.

title: Memory Controller Sensor Error
shortDescription: The memory controller detected a bad environmental sensor reading.
fullDescription:
Error 58.1 indicates a problem with the memory controller or an environmental sensor connected to it. On HP LaserJets, 58.xx typically points to an airflow or humidity sensor used by the engine to adjust print parameters.

The error may be accompanied by poor print quality. Causes include a failed sensor, wiring issues, or a bad DC controller board.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off for 5 minutes and power on.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate and reseat the environmental sensor per service manual.

whenToCallPro: If reseating does not resolve, the DC controller likely needs replacement.

faq.q: Does humidity cause this?
faq.a: Extreme humidity can trip the sensor momentarily. A power cycle clears transient cases.

title: Main Motor Timing Error
shortDescription: The main drive motor lost timing synchronization.
fullDescription:
Error 59.10 is a motor timing error indicating the main drive motor failed to achieve or maintain its encoder-tracked speed. The motor rotates the drum, developers, and transfer belt.

Causes include worn gears, a failed encoder, a disconnected motor cable, or a DC controller motor driver failure. Persistent 59.10 errors require motor or driver replacement.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Motor Cable
fixSteps.instruction: Remove rear cover, reseat main motor connector.

fixSteps.title: Replace Motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new OEM main motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: Gear train alignment often requires service manual and special tools.

faq.q: Does this damage other parts?
faq.a: Yes. Continued operation can strip gears and smear toner.

title: Fuser Motor Startup Error
shortDescription: The fuser motor failed to reach operating speed at startup.
fullDescription:
Error 59.30 indicates the fuser drive motor did not reach its target rotational speed within the expected window. The fuser motor rotates the fuser rollers that pull paper through the fusing section.

Causes include a jammed fuser, worn motor brushes (on DC motors), or a DC controller driver failure. Clearing a jam and power cycling often clears the error.

fixSteps.title: Check for Jam
fixSteps.instruction: Open the rear door and inspect the fuser for paper fragments.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Release the green levers, remove and reinstall the fuser.

fixSteps.title: Replace Motor
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, install replacement fuser motor.

whenToCallPro: If a new motor also fails, expect DC controller replacement.

faq.q: Can a paper jam cause this?
faq.a: Yes. A wedged scrap of paper inside the fuser can stall the motor and trigger 59.30.

title: Ink Cartridge Communication Failure
shortDescription: The printer cannot communicate with one or more ink cartridges.
fullDescription:
Error 0xC05D0281 is an HP inkjet error indicating the printer failed to communicate with a cartridge during startup or during a print job. It can involve any single cartridge or multiple.

Common causes are dirty cartridge contacts, an improperly seated cartridge, non-genuine cartridges that fail the authentication handshake, or a failed printhead. Cleaning the contacts and reseating the cartridges resolves most cases.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: Open the access door, remove each cartridge and firmly reinstall until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Clean Contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the copper contacts on each cartridge and inside the printer with a lint-free cloth lightly dampened with distilled water.

fixSteps.title: Replace Cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: If only one cartridge is flagged, swap it with a new genuine HP cartridge.

whenToCallPro: If contact cleaning and genuine cartridges fail, the printhead assembly needs service replacement.

faq.q: Can I use refilled cartridges?
faq.a: HP dynamic security may reject refilled or remanufactured cartridges, causing this error.

title: Ink System Catastrophic Failure
shortDescription: The printer reports a generic ink system failure requiring service.
fullDescription:
Error 0xC0070015 is a catastrophic ink system error on HP OfficeJet and ENVY printers. The firmware reports that the ink delivery system cannot be initialized, usually because of dried ink, a clogged printhead, or servicing station failure.

Recovery involves a thorough printhead clean, possibly removing the printhead and soaking the nozzle plate in warm distilled water. Many printers cannot be fully recovered and require replacement of the integrated printhead.

fixSteps.title: Deep Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Run the printer's deep cleaning cycle 2-3 times from the maintenance menu.

fixSteps.title: Manual Printhead Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the printhead and wipe the nozzle plate with a lint-free cloth and distilled water. Let dry before reinstalling.

fixSteps.title: Replace Printhead
fixSteps.instruction: Order a replacement printhead assembly for your model.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning fails and printhead replacement does not clear the error, the printer is likely beyond economical repair.

faq.q: Is replacing the printer cheaper?
faq.a: For entry-level OfficeJet and ENVY models yes - printhead kits cost nearly as much as a new printer.

title: Cartridge Failure Error
shortDescription: HP inkjet reports a cartridge failure preventing printing.
fullDescription:
Error 0x61BBFB12 is an HP inkjet cartridge failure indicating a cartridge has failed electronically or is unrecognized. The printer may identify which cartridge is at fault.

Try reseating and cleaning contacts first, then replace suspect cartridges with genuine HP units. A printer firmware reset sometimes clears stuck status flags.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinstall each cartridge until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Reset Printer
fixSteps.instruction: With cartridges installed, unplug the printer for 60 seconds, then plug in and power on.

fixSteps.title: Replace Cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: Swap cartridges one at a time to identify the failed unit.

whenToCallPro: If new cartridges fail too, the carriage contact harness may be damaged.

faq.q: Is this covered under warranty?
faq.a: If the printer is under warranty and genuine HP cartridges fail immediately, HP may cover repair.

title: OfficeJet Firmware Failure
shortDescription: HP OfficeJet printer reports a firmware or system error.
fullDescription:
Error 0xC6FD0113 on HP OfficeJet printers indicates a firmware failure, usually after an interrupted firmware update or a corrupted NVRAM. The printer may be stuck on the error screen, reboot repeatedly, or refuse network connections.

A forced firmware recovery via USB, followed by a semi-full reset, resolves most cases. In rare cases the formatter flash chip has failed and needs replacement.

fixSteps.title: Hard Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the printer for 2 minutes with cartridges still installed, then reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Semi-full Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power on while holding the # and 3 buttons (or as documented for your model) to enter service menu and run semi-full reset.

fixSteps.title: Firmware Recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Download the firmware recovery file from HP and apply via USB per the HP recovery guide.

whenToCallPro: If firmware recovery fails the formatter board must be replaced.

faq.q: Will I lose settings?
faq.a: Yes, a semi-full reset clears network and paper settings but preserves cartridge data.

title: DeskJet Printhead Error
shortDescription: HP DeskJet reports a printhead problem preventing printing.
fullDescription:
Error Oxc4eb827a on HP DeskJet models indicates the printhead is not recognized or has failed. It most often appears after a cartridge replacement or a power interruption during a print job.

Repeated power cycles with cartridges removed and reinstalled clears many cases. Manually cleaning the printhead with distilled water can recover clogged nozzles. A replacement printhead is needed in persistent cases.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle with Cartridges Out
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the printer, remove cartridges, unplug for 60 seconds, plug back in, power on, reinstall cartridges.

fixSteps.title: Manual Clean
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the printhead and gently dab the nozzle area with a cloth dampened with distilled water. Allow to dry.

fixSteps.title: Replace Printhead
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new printhead assembly for your model.

whenToCallPro: On entry-level DeskJets replacement is often not economical - a new printer may cost less.

faq.q: Can rubbing alcohol be used?
faq.a: No. Use only distilled water. Alcohol can damage the nozzle plate coating.

title: HP ENVY Stuck on Resetting
shortDescription: HP ENVY printer is stuck displaying 'Resetting' and will not finish initialization.
fullDescription:
HP ENVY printers can become stuck on a 'Resetting' screen after a firmware update, a hard reset, or a power outage during a print job. The firmware is attempting to restore defaults but cannot complete the process.

Pulling cartridges, performing a cold unplug of 15+ minutes, and reinserting typically clears the state. Semi-full and NVRAM resets via service menu are the next step. As a last resort, firmware recovery via USB is required.
symptoms: Power button only works to turn off

fixSteps.title: Cold Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the printer off, unplug it for 15 minutes with cartridges installed.

fixSteps.title: Carriage Check
fixSteps.instruction: Open the cartridge door and verify nothing is blocking the carriage. Move it gently by hand to the center.

fixSteps.title: Semi-full Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Enter the service menu (model-specific key combo) and run a semi-full reset.

whenToCallPro: If firmware recovery fails, the formatter board likely needs replacement.

faq.q: Will I lose ink levels?
faq.a: Yes, semi-full reset clears cartridge level tracking; the printer will re-sync once printing resumes.

title: HP ENVY Boot Loop
shortDescription: HP ENVY repeatedly reboots without finishing startup.
fullDescription:
A boot loop on HP ENVY printers means the unit repeatedly cycles power after showing the HP logo. This is typically firmware corruption, but can also be triggered by a stuck carriage or failed cartridge chip causing a watchdog reset.

Clearing obstructions, removing cartridges, and performing a cold unplug often breaks the loop. Firmware recovery over USB is the definitive fix for firmware-related boot loops.

fixSteps.title: Remove Cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: Take out all cartridges and try powering up.

fixSteps.title: Cold Unplug
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 15 minutes then try again.

fixSteps.title: Firmware Recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Connect to a PC via USB and run HP's firmware recovery utility for your ENVY model.

whenToCallPro: Formatter replacement is usually uneconomical for entry-level ENVY printers.

faq.q: Can a bad USB cable cause this?
faq.a: No, but a stuck firmware recovery attempt can. Use HP's official tool only.

title: Scanner Hardware Failure
shortDescription: The printer's scanner or ADF reports a hardware error.
fullDescription:
Error 0xC5D1295 on HP all-in-one printers indicates the scanner or ADF module failed initialization. Causes include a stuck scanner carriage, a failed CCD/CIS module, or a disconnected ribbon cable.

A cold power cycle frequently clears transient cases. Stuck carriages can be freed by gently moving the sled. Persistent errors require scanner assembly service.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Power off for 3 minutes and back on.

fixSteps.title: Free Carriage
fixSteps.instruction: Open the scanner lid and gently move the carriage by hand through its travel.

fixSteps.title: Replace Scanner Assembly
fixSteps.instruction: Install a replacement scanner module per service documentation.

whenToCallPro: Scanner ribbon cables are fragile; a service tech avoids damaging the formatter connectors.

faq.q: Can I still print?
faq.a: Printing may still work even when the scanner fails on all-in-ones.

title: Scanner Initialization Failure
shortDescription: Scanner failed to initialize at printer startup.
fullDescription:
0xC0020008 is an HP all-in-one error indicating the scanner could not complete its startup homing sequence. The carriage must find its home position; if the home sensor or drive belt fails the error is raised.

Clearing obstructions and a cold power cycle are the first steps. Persistent errors require inspection of the scanner drive belt, home sensor, and ribbon cable.

fixSteps.title: Remove Obstructions
fixSteps.instruction: Open the scanner and remove any objects, tape, or shipping locks.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the printer off for 2 minutes and power on.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Belt and Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the scanner glass assembly and inspect the drive belt and home sensor flag.

whenToCallPro: If belt or sensor replacement does not resolve, scanner assembly replacement is required.

faq.q: Is this caused by shipping?
faq.a: Yes, new units can trigger 0xC0020008 if the orange shipping lock on the scanner was not removed.

title: Low Sub-Thermistor Temperature
shortDescription: The fuser sub-thermistor detected abnormally low temperature during operation.
fullDescription:
Error 50.8 indicates the secondary (sub) thermistor on the fuser read a low temperature during normal operation. The main thermistor controls heating; the sub-thermistor acts as safety backup. A mismatch between the two raises 50.8.

Causes include a failed sub-thermistor, loose connector, or an aging fuser with uneven heating. Replacing the fuser maintenance kit clears the error.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Open rear cover and reseat the fuser assembly.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new fuser maintenance kit.

whenToCallPro: Unlikely unless DC controller also fails.

faq.q: Is 50.8 dangerous?
faq.a: No, it's a safety shutdown that prevents poor fusing.

title: Unexpected Paper Size in Tray
shortDescription: The printer detected a paper size different from the tray configuration.
fullDescription:
Error 41.3 means the printer's paper-size sensors measured a sheet that does not match the configured tray size. This halts the job to prevent wasting paper or jamming.

The fix is usually to align the paper guides accurately, reconfigure the tray in the control panel, or use the same paper size as the driver requests.

fixSteps.title: Align Guides
fixSteps.instruction: Pull out the tray, align guides snugly against the paper stack.

fixSteps.title: Reconfigure Tray
fixSteps.instruction: On the control panel, set the tray paper size to match the loaded paper.

whenToCallPro: Only if the paper size sensor itself is defective.

faq.q: Can I disable this?
faq.a: Yes, in the control panel paper handling menu you can disable size detection.

title: Supply Memory Read Failure
shortDescription: The printer cannot read the memory chip on the print cartridge.
fullDescription:
Error 10.00.00 means the printer cannot read the memory (e-label) chip on the toner cartridge. This chip stores cartridge identity, page count, and toner level.

Causes include a dirty contact point, a damaged chip, a non-genuine cartridge, or a failed reader assembly. Cleaning contacts and reseating usually clears the error.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and firmly reinstall the cartridge.

fixSteps.title: Clean Contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the cartridge chip and printer reader contacts with lint-free cloth.

fixSteps.title: Replace Cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: Swap in a genuine HP cartridge.

whenToCallPro: If genuine cartridges all report 10.00.00, the reader harness may need service.

faq.q: Do I need a new chip?
faq.a: No, the chip is built into the cartridge. Replace the cartridge instead.

title: Firmware Communication Error
shortDescription: The printer firmware encountered an unrecoverable error and must be restarted.
fullDescription:
Error 49.4C02 indicates the printer firmware received an invalid print job instruction or had an internal exception. It typically appears after sending a complex PCL/PostScript file that is malformed, a corrupted driver, or a network transmission error.

Power cycling the printer clears the current job. Updating firmware to the latest version prevents recurrence. Changing the driver from host-based to PCL6 sometimes helps with old applications.

fixSteps.title: Power Cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the printer off for 30 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Clear Queue
fixSteps.instruction: On the computer, cancel all pending print jobs before restarting.

fixSteps.title: Update Firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Download and install the latest firmware from HP support.

whenToCallPro: If 49 errors recur after firmware updates, the formatter RAM may be failing.

faq.q: Do I lose data?
faq.a: The current job is lost. Completed jobs and settings are preserved.

title: Fuser Overtemperature
shortDescription: The fuser temperature exceeded safe operating limits.
fullDescription:
Error 50.9 is a fuser overtemperature condition. The DC controller read a temperature above the safe threshold from either the main or sub thermistor and shut down heating to avoid fire.

Causes include a shorted thermistor, a stuck AC heater relay, or a runaway DC controller output. In all cases the fuser must be replaced before further use because thermal damage may have occurred.

Power cycle the printer; if the error clears briefly and returns, do not continue operating.

causes.cause: Stuck AC relay on DC controller

fixSteps.title: Stop Using Printer
fixSteps.instruction: Power off immediately and unplug the printer.

fixSteps.title: Replace Fuser
fixSteps.instruction: Install a new fuser maintenance kit before powering on again.

fixSteps.title: Service DC Controller
fixSteps.instruction: If the replacement fuser also overheats, the DC controller is defective and must be replaced by a technician.

whenToCallPro: If a replacement fuser still shows 50.9, the DC controller is unsafe and requires professional replacement.

faq.q: Is 50.9 a fire risk?
faq.a: Yes. Treat it seriously and do not continue running the printer until the fuser is replaced.

title: Firmware Critical Error 49.38.07
shortDescription: The printer firmware reported an unhandled exception and halted.
fullDescription:
Error 49.38.07 is a firmware exception on LaserJet Enterprise and Pro devices. The print controller encountered an unexpected state (often an invalid print job, corrupted font, or failed firmware update) and halted.

Typically clears with a cold reset. Persistent occurrences require a firmware reinstall.

causes.cause: Malformed PCL/PostScript data from a driver

fixSteps.title: Cold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Turn printer off, wait 30 seconds, turn back on.

fixSteps.title: Clear print queue
fixSteps.instruction: On each connected PC, open the print queue and cancel all jobs.

fixSteps.title: Update firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Download the latest firmware from HP and install via USB or EWS.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall driver
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and reinstall the printer driver using HP's full-feature installer.

whenToCallPro: If firmware reinstall does not clear the error, the formatter board may be failing.

faq.q: Is a single occurrence dangerous?
faq.a: No — a one-time 49.38.07 after a print job is normal and clears with a restart.

title: Unexpected Paper Type
shortDescription: The printer detected paper of an unexpected type during printing.
fullDescription:
Error 41.5 means the media sensor saw a paper type that does not match what the tray is configured for (e.g., a transparency where plain paper was expected). The printer pauses to avoid damage to the fuser.

Load the correct media or change the tray configuration in the control panel.

causes.cause: Tray configured for wrong paper type

symptoms: Job stops and requests correct paper

fixSteps.title: Check loaded paper
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the paper in the tray matches what the job requested.

fixSteps.title: Update tray settings
fixSteps.instruction: On the control panel, set the tray's paper type to match the loaded media.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensors
fixSteps.instruction: Blow out dust from the paper path sensors with compressed air.

whenToCallPro: If the error continues with plain paper loaded, the sensor has failed.

faq.q: Does this damage the printer?
faq.a: No, it is a protective stop.

title: Internal Communication Error
shortDescription: The formatter lost communication with the DC controller.
fullDescription: Error 42.0 indicates an internal I/O fault between the formatter and engine controller. Common causes are loose cables, failed firmware updates, or a damaged formatter.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 60 seconds, then reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cables
fixSteps.instruction: Remove side panels and reseat ribbon cables between formatter and DC controller.

fixSteps.title: Reflash firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Reflash the printer firmware via USB.

whenToCallPro: If reseating and firmware do not clear the fault, replace the formatter.

faq.q: Can I ignore this?
faq.a: No — it prevents all printing.

title: Digital Image Engine Error
shortDescription: Internal image-processing subsystem fault.
fullDescription:
47.XX errors (47.00, 47.01, 47.02, etc.) indicate a digital image engine fault — usually in the internal print engine CPU or image pipeline. The printer halts to avoid printing corrupt pages.

Most are cleared by power cycling; persistent faults require firmware or formatter service.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off, wait 60s, turn on.

fixSteps.title: Reload firmware
fixSteps.instruction: Install latest firmware via USB.

fixSteps.title: Call service
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, the formatter or engine board needs professional replacement.

whenToCallPro: Repeated 47.XX indicates hardware failure requiring technician.

faq.q: Is the page count reliable after?
faq.a: Yes, counters are preserved in separate NVRAM.

title: Scanner Motor Startup Failure
shortDescription: The laser scanner assembly failed to reach operating speed.
fullDescription:
Error 52.0XYZ (including 52.00, 52.01, 52.02) means the laser/scanner assembly failed to reach the correct rotational speed within the allowed time. This is required for proper laser timing.

Usually caused by a failed scanner motor, dirty mirror, or DC controller issue.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 60s, reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Reseat scanner cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open top cover, reseat the scanner ribbon cable.

fixSteps.title: Replace scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Order the correct laser/scanner unit and swap it in.

whenToCallPro: Scanner replacement requires careful alignment — professional recommended.

faq.q: Can I clean it instead of replace?
faq.a: If the failure is intermittent, cleaning the mirror and window can help — but a motor-speed fault usually means motor replacement.

title: Printer Fan Failure
shortDescription: One of the cooling fans has failed or is obstructed.
fullDescription: Error 57.XX covers all fan-related faults (57.01, 57.02, 57.03, 57.04). The DC controller detected that a fan is not rotating at required RPM. Fans cool the fuser, the formatter, and the power supply; operating without them risks thermal shutdown.

fixSteps.title: Power off and cool
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off and let cool for 15 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clean fans
fixSteps.instruction: Open rear panel and vacuum/blow out dust.

fixSteps.title: Test fan
fixSteps.instruction: With power on, check if fan spins; if not, replace.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Order correct fan for the model and swap.

whenToCallPro: If multiple fans fail simultaneously, the power supply or DC controller may be at fault.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep printing with fan error?
faq.a: No — overheating will damage the fuser.

title: DC Controller Power Error
shortDescription: The DC controller reported a power or environment fault.
fullDescription:
Error 58.XX (including 58.01, 58.02, 58.03, 58.04) points to a fault inside the DC controller, typically related to the environmental sensor or power supply communication.

Resetting often clears transient cases; persistent errors need DC controller replacement.

fixSteps.title: Cold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, unplug, wait 60s, reconnect.

fixSteps.title: Check ambient
fixSteps.instruction: Move printer to a normal-temperature environment (15-30C).

fixSteps.title: Replace DC controller
fixSteps.instruction: If error persists, the controller PCA must be replaced by a technician.

whenToCallPro: DC controller replacement is a professional repair.

faq.q: Does temperature really matter?
faq.a: Yes — the sensor reports ambient; extremes trigger protective shutdowns.

title: Motor Error (Generic)
shortDescription: One of the main drive motors failed to rotate correctly.
fullDescription:
Error 59.XX (59.F0, 59.A0, 59.B0, 59.C0, etc.) indicates that a main drive or toner motor is stalled, missing the startup signal, or drawing too much current.

Causes range from paper debris jamming a gear train to a failed motor.

causes.cause: Paper or debris jamming gear train

symptoms: Print stops at feed or fuser

fixSteps.title: Clear paper path
fixSteps.instruction: Open covers, remove any stuck paper, torn fragments, or debris.

fixSteps.title: Test motor
fixSteps.instruction: Enter service diagnostics and run motor test.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the specific motor indicated by the sub-code.

whenToCallPro: Motor replacement usually requires disassembly and alignment.

faq.q: How do I know which motor?
faq.a: The two digits after 59 identify the motor — consult the service manual for the specific model.

title: Carriage Jam (Left Stall)
shortDescription: The printhead carriage stalled toward the left side.
fullDescription: Error 0x6110003a appears on HP OfficeJet and ENVY inkjets when the carriage cannot move freely to the left. Usually caused by packaging tape, torn paper, or a stuck encoder strip.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Power off and unplug the printer.

fixSteps.title: Move carriage by hand
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, slide the carriage gently across the rail and check for resistance.

fixSteps.title: Clean encoder strip
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the clear plastic strip behind the carriage with a lint-free cloth and distilled water.

whenToCallPro: If encoder strip is torn, replacement requires partial disassembly.

faq.q: Can I print while this is showing?
faq.a: No, the carriage is blocked.

title: Carriage Jam (Right Stall)
shortDescription: The printhead carriage stalled toward the right side.
fullDescription: Error 0x6110004a is the right-side counterpart to 0x6110003a. The carriage failed to reach its right home position, typically due to something blocking the path or an encoder misread.

fixSteps.title: Inspect path
fixSteps.instruction: Open the access door and remove any debris.

fixSteps.title: Reset printer
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 60s, replug, power on.

fixSteps.title: Clean encoder
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe encoder strip with distilled water on a lint-free cloth.

whenToCallPro: Belt slippage needs professional retensioning.

faq.q: What if the carriage moves freely but error persists?
faq.a: The encoder sensor or strip is likely faulty.

title: Carriage Jam (Center Stall)
shortDescription: The printhead carriage stalled mid-travel.
fullDescription: Error 0x6110005a means the carriage stopped in the middle of its travel and could not continue. Often caused by cartridges not fully seated, a paper jam under the carriage, or an encoder error.

fixSteps.title: Reseat cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: Open the door and fully reseat each ink cartridge until it clicks.

fixSteps.title: Remove stuck paper
fixSteps.instruction: Look under carriage with a flashlight; remove any torn fragments.

fixSteps.title: Semi-full reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug with printer on for 60s, then replug.

whenToCallPro: If cartridges reseat but error continues, carriage belt or motor may have failed.

faq.q: Why did ink end up on the platen?
faq.a: The carriage may have dragged across a wet cartridge — clean the platen with a damp cloth.

title: Wireless Setup Service Error
shortDescription: The wireless configuration service crashed during setup.
fullDescription:
A '79 Service Error' appears on wireless-capable HP printers (DeskJet, ENVY, OfficeJet, Tango) when the embedded web service running the wireless setup wizard crashes. Related to memory fragmentation and old firmware.

Power cycle and firmware update resolve most cases.

fixSteps.title: Cold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, unplug for 60s, replug.

fixSteps.title: Restore network defaults
fixSteps.instruction: From Wireless > Settings > Restore Network Defaults.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Connect by USB and install the latest firmware.

whenToCallPro: If service errors persist across resets, contact HP — formatter replacement may be needed.

faq.q: Will I lose my printer settings?
faq.a: Only network and wireless settings — ink counters, page count, and firmware are preserved.

title: Generic Wireless Setup Failure
shortDescription: HP Smart displayed 'Something went wrong' during wireless setup.
fullDescription: A generic HP Smart app error shown when the phone or tablet could not complete wireless setup. Common on printers that briefly disconnect from Wi-Fi setup mode, or when the phone switches to a 5 GHz network the printer cannot see.

causes.cause: Phone on 5 GHz while printer needs 2.4 GHz
HP Smart app out of date

symptoms: Printer never appears in device list

fixSteps.title: Force phone to 2.4 GHz
fixSteps.instruction: On Android/iOS, turn off auto-switch 5 GHz or connect to a 2.4 GHz SSID.

fixSteps.title: Enable Bluetooth
fixSteps.instruction: Make sure Bluetooth is on during HP Smart setup.

fixSteps.title: Update HP Smart
fixSteps.instruction: Install latest HP Smart from the app store.

fixSteps.title: Reset printer network
fixSteps.instruction: Press Wi-Fi + Cancel for 5s to restore network defaults.

whenToCallPro: Rarely — this is almost always a setup-process issue.

faq.q: Do I need the app?
faq.a: For most modern HP printers, yes — initial setup uses HP Smart.

title: HP Smart App Communication Failure
shortDescription: HP Smart could not read printer status over the cloud.
fullDescription: Error 0x6100004A in HP Smart means the app cannot reach the printer to complete a print or scan request. Usually caused by printer offline, account not linked, or expired session.

fixSteps.title: Check printer online
fixSteps.instruction: Print a wireless test page from the printer.

fixSteps.title: Sign out/in
fixSteps.instruction: Sign out of the HP account in HP Smart and back in.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall app
fixSteps.instruction: Uninstall and reinstall HP Smart.

whenToCallPro: Very rare — most cases are app-side issues.

faq.q: Is cloud print secure?
faq.a: Yes — HP Smart uses TLS to communicate with the cloud.

title: HP Smart Scan Upload Failure
shortDescription: Scan-to-cloud upload failed from HP Smart.
fullDescription: Error 0x6100008A occurs when HP Smart successfully scans but cannot upload to cloud storage (OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox).

causes.cause: Cloud service disconnected in HP Smart

symptoms: Scan completes then fails to upload

fixSteps.title: Reconnect cloud
fixSteps.instruction: In HP Smart, remove and re-add the cloud service.

fixSteps.title: Check quota
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the cloud account has free space.

fixSteps.title: Retry scan
fixSteps.instruction: Retry the scan after reconnection.

whenToCallPro: No professional service needed.

faq.q: Does this affect local scan?
faq.a: No — you can still scan to the phone or computer locally.

title: Cartridge Chip Authentication Failed
shortDescription: A cartridge failed chip authentication.
fullDescription: Error B0001 (also seen as B0xxx family) indicates one of the installed cartridges has a chip the printer cannot authenticate. Common after firmware updates disable older or third-party cartridges.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the cartridge and clean the gold chip contacts with a dry lint-free cloth.

fixSteps.title: Reseat
fixSteps.instruction: Reinstall firmly until click.

fixSteps.title: Use HP cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: If a third-party cartridge, replace with a genuine HP cartridge for the model.

whenToCallPro: If genuine HP cartridge still fails, firmware downgrade may be required.

faq.q: Can I disable HP's Dynamic Security?
faq.a: Older firmware may allow it; newer printers do not.

title: Cartridge Chip Communication Error
shortDescription: The printer cannot communicate with a cartridge chip.
fullDescription: Error C0001 is a signal-level failure between the carriage contacts and the cartridge chip. Differs from B0001 (authentication) in that no data reaches the chip at all.

fixSteps.title: Remove and clean cartridge contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Use a lint-free cloth with distilled water.

fixSteps.title: Inspect carriage pins
fixSteps.instruction: Use a flashlight to check for bent or missing pins.

fixSteps.title: Replace cartridge
fixSteps.instruction: If pins look OK, try a new cartridge.

whenToCallPro: Bent pins require carriage repair by a technician.

faq.q: Does C0001 mean I need a new printhead?
faq.a: Not necessarily — usually contacts or a single cartridge.

title: Scanner Glass Error
shortDescription: The scanner could not calibrate against the document glass.
fullDescription: Error 22 on HP all-in-ones indicates the scanner CCD could not read its calibration strip beneath the document glass. Dirty glass or a misaligned scan bar is the usual cause.

fixSteps.title: Clean glass
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the glass with a microfiber cloth and glass cleaner.

fixSteps.title: Clean calibration strip
fixSteps.instruction: Open the lid and wipe the thin white strip on the glass edge.

fixSteps.title: Reset scanner
fixSteps.instruction: Power cycle the printer.

whenToCallPro: If scan bar is physically stuck, professional disassembly is needed.

faq.q: Do I need a special glass cleaner?
faq.a: No, ammonia-free glass cleaner or distilled water is fine.

title: Scanner Lamp Failure
shortDescription: The scanner lamp did not reach operating brightness.
fullDescription:
On HP MFPs, 'Scanner lamp error 49' (distinct from the 49.x firmware family) indicates the CCFL/LED scanner lamp failed or is too dim for proper calibration.

LEDs usually last the life of the unit — failure indicates driver issue or physical damage.

fixSteps.title: Reseat scanner cable
fixSteps.instruction: Open the scanner assembly and reseat the ribbon cable.

fixSteps.title: Test scan
fixSteps.instruction: Run a test scan from the control panel.

fixSteps.title: Replace scanner
fixSteps.instruction: If lamp is still dark, replace the scanner assembly.

whenToCallPro: Scanner assemblies are modular — professional replacement recommended.

faq.q: Can I replace just the lamp?
faq.a: No — HP scanners use an integrated lamp bar that is replaced as a unit.

title: Scanner Fan Failure
shortDescription: A fan in the scanner assembly failed to reach RPM.
fullDescription: Error 30.03 on HP LaserJet Enterprise MFPs indicates the scanner module's internal fan has failed. Not critical for printing but will block scan and copy functions.

fixSteps.title: Power off and cool
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off for 10 minutes.

fixSteps.title: Clean fan
fixSteps.instruction: Blow compressed air through the scanner vents.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: If fan does not spin, order replacement fan for MFP scanner.

whenToCallPro: If fan replacement fails, the ECU inside the scanner is faulty.

faq.q: Can I print without scan fan?
faq.a: Most models block all operation to protect scanner electronics.

title: Scanner System Error
shortDescription: The scanner system reported an unrecoverable fault.
fullDescription: Error 30.99 is a generic catch-all for scanner hardware faults on LaserJet Enterprise MFPs — used when the scanner controller reports an error that does not map to a specific sub-code.

fixSteps.title: Cold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power off for 60 seconds.

fixSteps.title: Firmware update
fixSteps.instruction: Install latest firmware to rule out software causes.

fixSteps.title: Service scanner
fixSteps.instruction: If persistent, schedule scanner service visit.

whenToCallPro: 30.99 usually requires professional scanner diagnostics.

faq.q: Does print still work?
faq.a: Yes, in most cases printing is unaffected.

title: Tray 2 Lift Motor Stall
shortDescription: The lift mechanism in Tray 2 failed to raise the paper stack.
fullDescription: Error 60.02 indicates that Tray 2's paper-lift motor did not raise the stack to pickup level within the allotted time. Common causes are overloaded tray, foreign object under the plate, or a failed motor.

fixSteps.title: Remove paper
fixSteps.instruction: Empty Tray 2 completely.

fixSteps.title: Inspect tray
fixSteps.instruction: Look for paper scraps under the lift plate and remove them.

fixSteps.title: Reload correctly
fixSteps.instruction: Load paper below the max-fill line.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: If still failing, replace the lift motor assembly.

whenToCallPro: Lift motor replacement in optional trays requires cassette removal and is straightforward for experienced users.

faq.q: Which tray is Tray 2?
faq.a: The first optional 500-sheet cassette below the main tray.

title: Photo Paper Alignment Fault
shortDescription: The printer could not align a photo print against the loaded media.
fullDescription: On HP Tango and ENVY Photo series, 'Photo Paper Align Fault' occurs when the alignment page cannot be scanned correctly. Caused by loading photo paper upside-down, plain paper substituted, or a dirty optical sensor.

fixSteps.title: Reload photo paper
fixSteps.instruction: Load glossy-side down in the photo tray.

fixSteps.title: Re-run alignment
fixSteps.instruction: From the control panel: Setup > Tools > Align Printhead.

fixSteps.title: Clean sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Blow compressed air into the paper exit area near the sensor window.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needed.

faq.q: Why must glossy face down?
faq.a: HP photo printers pull paper in and flip it during the photo print path.

title: Wireless Print Job Frozen in Queue
shortDescription: A job sent wirelessly is stuck in the queue and cannot be cleared.
fullDescription: A known HP Tango/ENVY behaviour: wireless print jobs can get stuck in the print queue if the printer lost Wi-Fi during transmission. New jobs also fail.

fixSteps.title: Restart spooler
fixSteps.instruction: Windows: Services > Print Spooler > Restart. Mac: Reset printing system.

fixSteps.title: Clear printer queue
fixSteps.instruction: On the printer: Settings > Printer Maintenance > Cancel All Jobs (if available), or power cycle.

fixSteps.title: Reconnect Wi-Fi
fixSteps.instruction: On the printer: re-run Wi-Fi Setup Wizard.

whenToCallPro: Rarely needs service.

faq.q: Do I need to reinstall the driver?
faq.a: Usually no — restarting the spooler is enough.

title: Laser Scanner Speed Error
shortDescription: The laser scanner motor reached speed but not accuracy.
fullDescription: Error 52.01 is a more specific variant of 52.XX: the scanner motor is rotating but not at the correct steady speed, causing horizontal banding or slow-start prints.

fixSteps.title: Cold reset
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug for 60s.

fixSteps.title: Clean mirror window
fixSteps.instruction: Open top cover and gently clean laser scanner window with a dry microfiber cloth.

fixSteps.title: Replace scanner
fixSteps.instruction: If print quality does not recover, replace scanner assembly.

whenToCallPro: Scanner motor replacement is professional work.

faq.q: Why do I see banding?
faq.a: Because scanning is uneven at that motor speed.

title: Environment Temperature Warning
shortDescription: Ambient temperature outside allowed range.
fullDescription: Error 58.02 is raised when the DC controller's environmental sensor reads a temperature outside the operating range (10-32C typical). Moving the printer to a controlled room usually resolves.

causes.cause: Printer in cold garage or hot room

symptoms: Printer refuses to print until warmed up

fixSteps.title: Relocate printer
fixSteps.instruction: Move printer to a climate-controlled room.

fixSteps.title: Allow acclimation
fixSteps.instruction: Leave printer powered off for 30 minutes in new environment.

fixSteps.title: Test
fixSteps.instruction: Power on and run a test page.

whenToCallPro: If temperature is normal but error persists, sensor replacement is a technician job.

faq.q: Minimum operating temperature?
faq.a: HP specifies 10C (50F) — colder environments may trigger 58.02.

title: Developer Motor Error
shortDescription: The developer unit motor failed to rotate correctly.
fullDescription: Error 59.A0 indicates the developer motor (which drives toner into the drum) stalled or drew abnormal current. Common in LaserJet Enterprise color models.

fixSteps.title: Remove cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: Remove all toner cartridges and check for resistance when rotating gears.

fixSteps.title: Clean area
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum any loose toner inside the printer.

fixSteps.title: Run motor test
fixSteps.instruction: Enter service diagnostics and test developer motor.

fixSteps.title: Service
fixSteps.instruction: Replace motor if still failing.

whenToCallPro: Developer motor replacement requires partial disassembly — professional recommended.

faq.q: Can I keep using with 59.A0?
faq.a: No — it prevents any printing.

title: ITB Drive Motor Error
shortDescription: Intermediate transfer belt drive motor fault.
fullDescription: Error 59.B0 indicates a fault in the intermediate transfer belt (ITB) drive motor or related feedback signals in color LaserJets.

fixSteps.title: Remove ITB
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the intermediate transfer belt assembly per service manual.

fixSteps.title: Inspect drive
fixSteps.instruction: Rotate the drive gear by hand — any resistance suggests motor failure.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace drive motor or ITB assembly.

whenToCallPro: ITB work is professional — alignment is critical.

faq.q: Will this damage the ITB?
faq.a: If the belt is jammed against a failed motor, yes — inspect carefully.

title: ENVY Printer Stuck at Initializing
shortDescription: The ENVY printer shows 'Initializing' indefinitely on power-up.
fullDescription: A known issue on HP ENVY and Tango series where the printer boots but never completes initialization, staying on the startup/splash screen. Usually firmware hang or power supply issue.

fixSteps.title: Hard reset
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, unplug for 60 seconds, unplug USB and network, power on alone.

fixSteps.title: Test power adapter
fixSteps.instruction: Swap adapter with another HP printer of same model.

fixSteps.title: Firmware recovery
fixSteps.instruction: Use HP's firmware recovery tool over USB.

whenToCallPro: If firmware recovery fails, mainboard replacement needed.

faq.q: How long to wait?
faq.a: If >5 minutes on 'Initializing' it is hung.

title: HP ePrint / Cloud Print Failed
shortDescription: A cloud print job did not reach the printer.
fullDescription: When emailing to the printer's HP ePrint address or sending via HP Smart cloud, the job can silently fail. Causes include: printer offline, ePrint service disabled, attachment too large, or account not linked.

fixSteps.title: Print internet report
fixSteps.instruction: Settings > Web Services > Print Info Page.

fixSteps.title: Enable Web Services
fixSteps.instruction: Ensure Web Services is on and printer is registered.

fixSteps.title: Reduce attachment
fixSteps.instruction: Split large PDFs into smaller files.

whenToCallPro: Cloud issues rarely need service.

faq.q: Why are some attachments blocked?
faq.a: HP ePrint limits attachment size (typically 10MB) and blocks unsupported formats.

title: 54.10 Color Density Sensor Error
shortDescription: Failure of the color density / registration sensor.
fullDescription: Error 54.10 indicates the color density sensor cannot read the calibration patches. Toner contamination on the sensor or transfer belt issues are common causes.

fixSteps.title: Clean density sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Locate sensor near ITB and gently clean with lint-free cloth.

fixSteps.title: Run color calibration
fixSteps.instruction: From the menu, run the full color calibration.

fixSteps.title: Inspect ITB
fixSteps.instruction: Check transfer belt for streaks or damage.

whenToCallPro: ITB replacement should be performed by a technician.

faq.q: Is calibration enough?
faq.a: Often yes after cleaning the sensor.

faq.q: How often should I calibrate?
faq.a: Every 2,000 pages or after toner changes.

title: 56.10 Input Tray Communication Error
shortDescription: Optional paper tray cannot communicate with the printer.
fullDescription: Error 56.10 indicates the printer detected an optional input tray but cannot establish communication. Reseating the tray and checking pogo-pin connectors usually fixes it.

fixSteps.title: Reseat tray
fixSteps.instruction: Power off, slide optional tray out and firmly back in.

fixSteps.title: Clean contacts
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe pogo pins with a dry cloth.

fixSteps.title: Test without tray
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the tray, boot, then re-add to confirm.

whenToCallPro: If the tray itself is dead, replacement is required.

faq.q: Is the tray under warranty?
faq.a: If purchased recently, check HP warranty status.

faq.q: Can I run without the optional tray?
faq.a: Yes — main tray functions normally.

title: 57.07 Cartridge Fan Error
shortDescription: The cartridge cooling fan has failed or is obstructed.
fullDescription: Error 57.07 reports the cartridge fan is not turning at expected RPM. Dust or a worn bearing are typical causes; the fan is field-replaceable on most enterprise models.

fixSteps.title: Power off and inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Power down and visually inspect fan for obstruction.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum dust
fixSteps.instruction: Use an electronics-safe vacuum to clear debris.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Install a replacement fan kit.

whenToCallPro: Replacement requires partial disassembly — call a tech if uncomfortable.

faq.q: Why is fan critical?
faq.a: It cools the cartridge — without it toner can melt.

faq.q: Can I run briefly without it?
faq.a: No — printer locks out for safety.

title: 58.04 Power Supply Voltage Error
shortDescription: Low-voltage power supply is reporting an out-of-range voltage.
fullDescription: Error 58.04 indicates the LVPS is providing voltages outside spec. This may be caused by line-voltage problems or a failing supply. Persistent errors usually require LVPS replacement.

fixSteps.title: Test on a different outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Move printer to a known-good circuit.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 5 minutes, restart.

fixSteps.title: Service replacement
fixSteps.instruction: Have a technician test/replace the LVPS.

whenToCallPro: LVPS work requires high-voltage safety — pro recommended.

faq.q: Is this dangerous?
faq.a: Don't open the LVPS — capacitors store dangerous voltage.

faq.q: Could a UPS cause it?
faq.a: Yes — try a wall outlet first.

title: 59.20 Main Motor Startup Failure
shortDescription: The main drive motor failed to start.
fullDescription: Error 59.20 reports the main motor did not reach speed at startup. Mechanical jams, worn motor, or a controller fault are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Clear all paper
fixSteps.instruction: Open every door and remove any paper or debris.

fixSteps.title: Rotate gears manually
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, gently rotate visible gears to check for binds.

fixSteps.title: Replace main motor
fixSteps.instruction: Schedule service-tech replacement.

whenToCallPro: Motor replacement requires partial teardown.

faq.q: Will the printer self-recover?
faq.a: Sometimes after clearing paper — try a power cycle.

faq.q: Is grinding normal?
faq.a: No — grinding indicates a stuck gear or worn motor.

title: 62.00 No System Found
shortDescription: The printer cannot find a valid firmware image.
fullDescription: Error 62.00 indicates the firmware image on the formatter is missing or corrupt. A firmware reload via USB or service mode usually restores operation.

fixSteps.title: USB firmware load
fixSteps.instruction: Boot into recovery and apply firmware via USB drive.

fixSteps.title: NVRAM init

title: Paper Stopped at Top of Page Sensor
shortDescription: Paper has stopped at the top-of-page sensor and the printer cannot continue.
fullDescription: Error 13.20.01 indicates the paper has been picked up but stopped at the registration / top-of-page sensor before reaching the fuser. The most common causes are worn registration rollers, a damaged top-of-page sensor flag, or torn paper still inside the print path.

causes.cause: Torn paper fragment near registration sensor

symptoms: Print job halts with paper inside printer
Paper visible at the registration assembly when opening the front cover
Repeat jams in the same location

fixSteps.title: Power Down and Inspect
fixSteps.instruction: Turn the printer off and open all access covers. Carefully remove any paper or debris from the registration area.

fixSteps.title: Clean Registration Rollers
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe registration rollers with a lint-free cloth lightly dampened with isopropyl alcohol. Let dry fully.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor Flag
fixSteps.instruction: Manually flick the top-of-page sensor flag and confirm it springs back. Replace the sensor assembly if sluggish.

fixSteps.title: Run Paper Path Test
fixSteps.instruction: From the service menu, run the paper path test page to confirm no further jams.

whenToCallPro: Call a technician if jams persist after roller cleaning and sensor inspection — the registration assembly may need replacement.

faq.q: Is 13.20.01 the same as a generic paper jam?
faq.a: It's a specific subset — paper made it past the pickup but stopped at the registration sensor.

faq.q: Can low-quality paper cause this?
faq.a: Yes. Curled, damp, or undersized paper often triggers 13.20 family errors.

title: Paper Late to Top-of-Page Sensor
shortDescription: Paper did not reach the top-of-page sensor in time.
fullDescription: Error 13.20.02 indicates that paper was picked from the tray but did not reach the top-of-page sensor within the expected window. This is usually caused by slipping pickup or feed rollers.

causes.cause: Paper too heavy for selected tray

symptoms: Audible roller spin without paper advancement
Random jam frequency increases over time

fixSteps.title: Inspect Pickup Roller
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the tray and check the pickup roller for shiny / glazed surface. Replace if worn.

fixSteps.title: Replace Separation Pad
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the tray separation pad if it appears compressed or smooth.

fixSteps.title: Verify Paper Settings
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm media type in driver matches loaded paper — using Plain when Heavy is loaded causes slip.

whenToCallPro: If new rollers don't fix the issue, the pickup clutch or solenoid likely needs service.

faq.q: Will replacing all rollers help?
faq.a: Yes — replacing the full maintenance kit at the recommended page count usually resolves this family of errors.

fullDescription: Error 13.20.03 occurs when paper enters the fuser but does not clear the fuser exit sensor in time. This is often caused by a worn fuser, damaged exit roller, or paper stuck inside the fuser sleeve.

fixSteps.title: Power Down and Cool

fixSteps.title: Remove Stuck Paper
fixSteps.instruction: Open the rear door and pull paper straight through the fuser path.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Fuser Sleeve

whenToCallPro: Fuser replacement involves high-voltage components — call a pro if uncomfortable opening the rear assembly.

faq.q: How long does a fuser last?

title: Ink System Failure
shortDescription: The HP printer detected a problem with the ink delivery system that is preventing printing.
fullDescription: Error 0xc19a0003 indicates the printer's ink system has failed self-diagnostic checks. This typically points to a clogged printhead, dried ink in the delivery tubes, or failed pressure sensors in the ink supply station.

Air bubble in ink supply line

symptoms: Printer displays 'Ink System Failure' on screen
Cleaning cycle does not resolve issue
Streaks or missing colors before failure

fixSteps.title: Power Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off the printer, unplug for 60 seconds, then power back on with cartridges installed.

fixSteps.title: Clean Printhead
fixSteps.instruction: Run printhead cleaning cycle 2-3 times from printer maintenance menu.

fixSteps.title: Reseat Cartridges
fixSteps.instruction: Remove all cartridges, wipe contacts with lint-free cloth, reinsert firmly.

fixSteps.title: Manual Printhead Soak
fixSteps.instruction: Remove printhead, soak nozzle plate in warm distilled water for 10 minutes, dry and reinstall.

whenToCallPro: If error persists after printhead replacement, the ink system electronics or main logic board may need professional diagnosis.
